subject: Procurement playbook: hosting decision criteria & next steps
messages:
From: Samir Rao <samir@averytech.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up from today's discovery — procurement questions

Hi Irene,

Thanks for the call this morning — Samir here from Avery. Helpful session; appreciate Marcus walking through the latency/cost tradeoffs. A few follow-ups from procurement that will determine our path: 

- Payment method: they want to confirm if Redwood accepts PO (net-30) for annual reserved commitments, or if card-only applies to on-demand.
- Marketplace: procurement asked whether buying through the cloud marketplace (GCP Marketplace) is an option for billing and consolidated invoicing.
- Security evidence: they need an audit scope list (SOC 2 controls, encryption in transit/at rest) for legal.

A couple of asks from my side: if we choose Dedicated (reserved) with a 12-month commit, would PO be fully supported? If not, what are the billing options? Also curious about any differences in pricing if we buy via marketplace versus direct contract.

I've attached the SOW draft procurement sent over for reference (avery_sow_draft.pdf).

Looking forward to a quick summary so I can feed this back to my CFO and procurement team.

Best,
Samir
Procurement Lead
Avery Technologies

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Samir Rao <samir@averytech.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up from today's discovery — procurement questions

Samir — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers up-front, then a short next-steps plan: 

1) Payment methods
- Reserved (Dedicated) with a term commitment: we support PO (net-30) for customers who sign an MSA + committed capacity contract. Procurement will need to sign the commercial addendum.
- On-demand / Hosted pay-as-you-go: card is the standard; we can accept ACH for larger invoices but POs on pure on-demand are uncommon.

2) Marketplace
- We do list select SKUs on GCP Marketplace and AWS Marketplace in certain regions. Marketplace purchases route through the cloud partner and change invoicing and support workflows (you get consolidated cloud billing). Pricing via marketplace can differ (sometimes list-to-catalog mapping results in different discount mechanics).

3) Security evidence
- I'll loop Monica (security/compliance liaison) to provide the SOC 2 scope summary and encryption details.

Proposed immediate next steps:
- I will send a one-page procurement playbook that maps purchase method (PO vs card, marketplace vs direct) against the hosting choice (Hosted, Dedicated, Private) and the expected procurement timeline.
- Marcus will pull the hosting-comparison workbook and call out price delta estimates for the Avery workload profile you shared.
- If procurement prefers PO on Dedicated, we can provision a draft commercial addendum for PO terms and share the contract redlines.

Can we schedule a 30-min sync Thursday 8/27 at 10am PT to align on the Purchase path? If that works, I will invite our finance lead.

Irene Choi
Senior Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference

---
Attachment: redwood-hosting-comparison.xlsx (pricing + configuration workbook)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Samir Rao <samir@averytech.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 13:44:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up from today's discovery — procurement questions

Samir — sharing the quick delta analysis I promised. Highlights from the workbook: 

- Hosted (on-demand) — lowest time-to-value; estimated monthly run-rate for your observed usage: $5.4k/month. No commit required. Card or ACH recommended.
- Dedicated (12-month commit) — ~30% unit price improvement versus hosted when we size to expected concurrency; requires committed monthly min spend -> PO (net-30) supported once contract is in place.
- Private (VPC/on-prem) — highest up-front ops and setup; suitable if Avery needs on-prem control or specific regulatory isolation. Billing typically via invoice + PO, and implementation SOW applies.

I've attached the slice of the workbook with the modeled scenarios and conservative utilization assumptions. Please note marketplace purchases typically show different invoice timing and sometimes add a marketplace fee; net landed price varies.

Let's confirm the Thursday slot if that works and we'll prepare a short playbook and contract starter for procurement to review.

Marcus Lin
Solution Architect, Redwood Inference

---
Attachment: redwood-hosting-comparison.xlsx (sheet: Avery_scenarios)

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 26 Aug 2026 15:38:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up from today's discovery — procurement questions

Samir — Monica here from Trust & Compliance. Per your SOC 2 and encryption ask: attached is the summary we can share with procurement (non-sensitive controls summary). If procurement needs deeper artifacts (full SOC 2 report), we can start an NDA + secure transfer workflow.

Key items for procurement checklist: 
- Billing path: Confirm if Avery prefers consolidated cloud billing (marketplace) vs Redwood direct contract. If direct + PO: expect a 10–14 business day procurement review on average.
- Contract: we will provide a commercial addendum that enables PO terms for committed Dedicated contracts. If you want a standard PO without commit, that will need finance approval (and pricing will be closer to on-demand).
- Procurement docs we can provide immediately: SOC2 summary, encryption at rest/in transit, subprocessor list, and the standard security questionnaire mapping.

I've uploaded a redlines file with comments on sections we typically see edited by procurement (pricing table, termination, data retention) — named avery_redlines.docx. If you can share procurement's preferred contact and any SOW redlines they want prioritized, we'll incorporate them into the draft contract.

Finally — Thursday 8/27 10:00am PT works for our side. I'll send a calendar invite with a short agenda: 1) Purchase path decision, 2) Timeline for PO + contract, 3) Security evidence handoff.

Best,
Monica Patel
Trust & Compliance Liaison
Redwood Inference
